data.title: Moomoo steps up Australian expansion with Sydney Roosters deal, second retail store
data.description:
SYDNEY, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Moomoo Australia and New Zealand today announced its largest local brand investment to date, signing on as platinum partner and official share-trading platform of the Sydney Roosters from the 2027 NRL season.

The deal coincides with the opening of Moomoo's second retail store, in Melbourne's eastern hub of Box Hill, marking one year since the brokerage opened its first physical site in Chatswood, Sydney.

Together, the moves cap four years of rapid local growth, signalling a broader push into mainstream retail and high-net-worth investing. Named Australia's most-trusted investing app in Finder's 2026 customer satisfaction awards, moomoo has also held the top spot as the nation's most-downloaded share-trading app for two consecutive years.*

Sydney Roosters partnership

From the 2027 season, the moomoo logo will appear on the sternum of the Roosters' NRL jersey and the front of their playing shorts, supported by match-day and community activations across Sydney.

"Partnering with a club of the Sydney Roosters' calibre reflects our long-term commitment to the Australian market," said Moomoo Australia and New Zealand chief executive officer Michael McCarthy. "Combining tier-one sporting visibility with face-to-face support in our stores helps build the familiarity and trust everyday Australians want before putting their money to work."

Easts Group chief executive officer Joe Kelly welcomed the announcement. "We’re delighted to welcome moomoo to the Sydney Roosters as our platinum partner and official share-trading platform," he said. "Moomoo is an ambitious, forward-thinking brand with a clear vision for its future. We see a strong alignment between its ambitions and the Roosters’ commitment to performance."

An expanding presence

Since launching locally in 2022, Moomoo Australia and New Zealand has steadily expanded its physical and market presence. Alongside the new Box Hill store and further outlets planned for 2027, the brokerage recently launched Moomoo Priority for high-net-worth users and hosted its inaugural Australian investor day in partnership with Nasdaq. Across Australia and New Zealand the firm’s local headcount will reach 70 staff by the end of 2026.

About moomoo

Moomoo Securities Australia Ltd, a Sydney-based, wholly owned subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed Futu Holdings Ltd, operates the moomoo platform across Australia and New Zealand. The moomoo app gives users access to more than 10,000 shares and exchange-traded funds across the Australian, US and Hong Kong sharemarkets, with US brokerage starting from US99¢ per trade, 24 hours every trading day. The platform pairs low-cost execution with real-time Level 2 US market data, advanced charting, an AI-powered assistant, curated financial news and user forums.

*Source: Sensor Tower, brokerage app downloads in Australia from January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. Combined total downloads for the moomoo app on Australian iOS and Android stores (referring to the moomoo global app from January 1, 2025 to November 7, 2025, and the Moomoo Australia app from November 7, 2025 onwards). Ranking may change over time.

A photo accompanying this announcement is available at https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/AttachmentNg/e2a79f52-42cd-4240-872a-96c9f2a00871

CONTACT: Media Contact: Carlee Snyder pr@us.moomoo.com

data.title: AI Selloff Spreads From Wall Street To Asia Despite Anthropic Debut: SPY, QQQ, DIA, Asian Stocks Head For Steep Weekly Losses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Choppy technology trades amid Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO suppressed liquidity across the board as investors freed up capital to invest in the new AI company on the block.
  • The Taiex in Taiwan plunged nearly 6%, putting the benchmark on course for its worst week since 1991.
  • According to Rajat Agarwal, an Asia equity strategist with Societe Generale, the sharp selloff across the AI sector reflects worries that AI-led growth is slowing down and the “peak growth phase” may have passed.

Global stock markets are headed for a steep red close this week despite Claude-maker Anthropic’s (ANT) record debut on the Nasdaq.

While ANT stock jumped more than 17% on its listing on Thursday, the rest of the U.S. markets took a beating, adding pressure to an already challenging week across the board.

Asian markets, including China, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, also slumped on fears of the unsustainability of the AI boom, and inflation concerns spread far and wide.

US Markets Vs Asia Markets

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100, are poised to end the week more than 5% lower, while the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) is headed for a decline over 6% this week.

Choppy technology trades amid Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO suppressed liquidity across the board as investors freed up capital to invest in the new AI company on the block. Even Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) strong third-quarter results failed to boost sentiment.

Much like Wall Street, Asia’s main bourses also witnessed a bloodbath, slumping severely at the open on Friday. Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 and Seoul’s KOSPI each plunged about 4.5% in the morning trading. The Taiex in Taiwan plunged nearly 6%, putting the benchmark on course for its worst week since 1991.

The iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF (EWT) has been hit the worst this week, losing nearly 14% so far. The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) is also down nearly 6% as the heavily AI-weighted market witnessed a steep selloff in SK Hynix and Samsung, following the AI rout in the U.S.

Meanwhile, the iShares MSCI China ETF (MCHI), and the iShares MSCI Japan ETF (EWJ) are also headed more than 5% lower this week.

Tech Stocks Have Plunged This Week

Among major tech stocks, U.S.-listed shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) have tumbled nearly 12% this week, while American shares of SK Hynix Inc. (SKHY) have lost more than 9.5% of their value so far.

Samsung, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) and NVDA shares have also taken a beating amid the tech rout.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) is down 10.43%. This is despite the exchange-traded fund drawing more than $13.1 billion year-to-date, on track for its largest annual intake on record, as per The Kobeissi Letter. This month alone, SMH has attracted +$2.2 billion, putting the fund on track for its largest monthly inflow since the +$3.2 billion recorded in July.

Meanwhile, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) is down about 10% this week. As per The Kobeissi Letter, U.S. technology stock valuations have hit their lowest level since March 2020 amid the market correction.

Anthropic’s Record IPO Crunches Liquidity

Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday much above its allocation price of $83. ANT stock soared more than 17% at close, ending the session at $97.17 and taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion.

“The listing of Anthropic failing to lift the market sentiment is the main hit on AI across Asia,” Steven Leung, executive director at UOB Kay Hian Hong Kong Ltd. told Bloomberg.

“Short sellers are seeing no improvement in downside pressure, so there no rush to cover their short positions,” Leung added.

Is AI Trade Running Out Of Growth Catalysts?

According to Rajat Agarwal, an Asia equity strategist with Societe Generale, the sharp selloff across the AI sector reflects worries that AI-led growth is slowing down and the “peak growth phase” may have passed. “The second element is on the demand vacuum that we are seeing,” Agarwal told Al Jazeera.

“At the time when foreigners are not buying, it is to be seen how long can the domestic investors stay put, particularly in Korea, on which the drawdown has been more severe,” he added.

Meanwhile, analyst Michaël van de Poppe said in a post on X that ANT stock would eventually see a selloff after its run-up in the first few days, after which liquidity would rotate toward other risk-on assets.

“I would expect to see $NQ, $BTC and other assets to rally upwards from that liquidity injection alongside a drop in Oil and the Yields,” he said.

Retail Stance: US Vs Asia Markets

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SPY slipped from ‘bullish’ to ‘neutral’ at the time of writing, while it was ‘bullish’ for QQQ. Sentiment around DIA slipped to ‘bearish’ territory.

Meanwhile, retail sentiment around EWJ was ‘bullish,’ while it was ‘neutral’ for MCHI and EWY. Sentiment around EWT was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing.

data.title: Neugebauer: Texas Court Ruling on Fermi's 70/30 Boardroom Maneuver Is a Loss for 100% of Texas Shareholders
data.description:
• Neugebauer: Under this ruling, the board can entrench itself with one quick vote, while shareholders need 70% of all outstanding shares to fight back.
  • Neugebauer: "That isn't Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."
  • Directors who failed to win a majority on October 30 are still sitting in the boardroom.
  • Neugebauer filing appeal because Texas's standing as the best place to do business in America depends on getting this right.
  • Texan voters have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them.

DALLAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Toby Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc. (d/b/a Fermi America) (Nasdaq: FRMI) ("Fermi" or the "Company"), today issued the following statement after the Texas Business Court dismissed his claims in Neugebauer v. Fermi Inc. challenging the 70% supermajority bylaw the Company's board adopted in May without a shareholder vote.

"This isn't just a loss for Melissa and me. I believe it's a loss for every shareholder of every Texas company," said Toby Neugebauer. "Under this ruling, a board can change the rules in the middle of a fight, without a shareholder vote. It takes the board one quick vote to change the rules. It takes shareholders 70% of all outstanding shares to have a voice. Do the math. A little over 30% can block anything, and a share that is never voted counts as a no.

"Directors who could not win a majority of the shareholder support are still sitting in the boardroom. I don't think that is Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."

On May 13, 2026, in the middle of a shareholder contest, Fermi's board amended the Company's bylaws. Under the amendment, shareholders now need 70% of all outstanding shares to expand the board or change how the bylaws are amended. The board, however, can change those same rules with a simple majority vote of its directors. In August, the board changed director elections to require a majority of all outstanding shares, with unvoted shares counting as a no vote. At the October 30 annual meeting, neither director on the ballot reached that majority. Both men remain on the board.

"I'm proud of the work Texas has done to become the best place in America to do business," Neugebauer continued. "But capital flows to boards that answer to their owners. If shareholders can be silenced whenever a board disagrees with them, investors will notice."

This November, voters rejected the insider, pay-to-play politics that has harmed Fermi. Texans have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them. We respectfully disagree with the Court and feel confident that we will be successful on appeal, because this isn't how good governance works.

Texas earned its business reputation. Now it has to protect it. I will continue to advocate for good governance, not for financial gain, but for the good of Texas.

data.title: Treasury rally spills over to Indian bonds, debt supply slows move
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds were marginally higher in early deals on Friday, tracking a rise in US Treasuries, while the major focus shifted to fresh supply through the weekly debt auction, with the cutoffs set to drive the markets later in the day.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield was at 7.2439% as of 10 a.m. IST, after closing at 7.2543% on Thursday.

New Delhi will sell bonds worth 330 billion rupees ($3.54 billion), including the liquid five-year paper.

"Bulls are trying their best to drag yields further down, but some profit-taking and caution before the auction is not allowing any major rally," trader with a primary dealership said.

"The real direction will probably emerge later, once the cutoff is known."

US Treasury yields eased on Thursday as a sharp selloff in US equities prompted investors to move into safe-haven government bonds.

The decline in yields also comes against a softer economic backdrop and traders are increasingly pricing in the possibility that the Federal Reserve will take a more measured approach at its December meeting.

According to CME FedWatch data, the probability of a 50-basis-point hike has dropped to about 3%, after briefly rising as high as 14% earlier in the week.

The benchmark Brent crude remains around $92 a barrel, but oil prices continue to be highly sensitive to developments around the Strait of Hormuz, and any prolonged disruption in the region could rapidly tighten global supplies.

For India, higher oil prices remain a key macroeconomic risk, as it impacts the nation's current account deficit, local currency and inflation trajectory.

Markets have therefore positioned for the Reserve Bank of India to potentially deliver another rate increase in early December, after India's retail inflation moved above the 6% upper tolerance threshold for the first time in two years.

RATES

Overnight index swap rates were down, but trading volumes remained thing.

The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate was at 6.46%, while the two-year rate (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) was not yet traded. The more liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate was at 6.48%.

($1 = 93.2900 Indian rupees)

data.title: India's Embassy Developments buys out US joint venture partner
data.description:
Indian property developer Embassy Developments (BSE: 532832) has completed its purchase of the remaining 50% of Embassy Columbia Pacific ASL Private Limited from US-based CP Senior Housing (India) LLC, the company told stock exchanges in a filing on November 19.

The deal ends a joint venture in which each partner held half the equity. Embassy Columbia is now a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bengaluru-based group, formerly known as Equinox India Developments. The change took effect on November 19. Embassy Developments paid INR326.5mn ($3.499mn) for 11,244,599 equity shares with a face value of INR10 each. The shares made up the whole of CP Senior's holding in the company. The developer said it transferred the payment once the closing conditions set out in the share purchase agreement had been met.

The two sides signed that agreement on October 29. Embassy Developments disclosed the transaction to the exchanges on the same date. According to the filing, the details required under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's listing rules, referred to in the document as the 'SEBI LODR Regulations', were all contained in the October 29 disclosure. The company said nothing in those details had changed apart from the completion of the acquisition.

data.title: Indian stocks pause near nine-month highs; Asia market rout deepens
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran

Indian shares hovered near nine-month highs on Friday, bucking a broader Asian selloff as Anthropic's market debut failed to revive confidence in AI-linked stocks.

The Nifty 50 added 0.09% to 25,537.15, while the Sensex gained 0.07% to 83,074.37 as of 9:59 a.m. IST.

Nine of the 16 major sectors declined. Small-caps lost 0.4% and mid-caps traded flat.

Metals dropped 1.8% on concerns over AI-related demand and a stronger dollar.

IT stocks gained 2%, recovering from a 3.2% decline over the previous three sessions.

Despite the muted start to the session, the Nifty and Sensex are up 1.5% and 1.8% this week, on course for their fourth straight weekly gain, helped by a record $12.21 billion of monthly foreign inflows on AI-trade unwind, easing crude oil prices and upbeat earnings.

Asian markets on the other hand are on track for their worst week since 2020. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares (.MISX00000PUS) lost 2.5% on Friday as strong demand for Anthropic shares failed to carry through to gains in shares of AI supply chain companies.

"India is the only high-performing market in the world this month with the Nifty surging 10.7% in just 13 trading days," said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments.

"Profit booking is happening in the market, but the FII buying is so sustained and aggressive that the bulls are calling the shots."

Among stocks, Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals jumped 4% each after Macquarie double-upgraded the two companies to "outperform" from "underperform" and raised price targets, citing an improving earnings outlook.

Dilip Buildcon rose 3.7% after receiving order worth 4.19 billion rupees from Gurugram Metro Rail for the Gurugram Metro Corridor project.

Ashoka Buildcon fell 4% after it said Saudi Arabia's Diriyah Company canceled a project worth 8.46 billion rupees due to internal reasons.

data.title: Nifty IT jumps over 1% as TCS, Tech Mahindra, HCL Tech gain; Indian IT stocks buck global AI selloff
data.description:
Indian information technology stocks rallied on Friday, defying a sharp selloff in global technology shares and weakness across most domestic sectors. The Nifty IT index climbed more than 1 percent, with TCS, Tech Mahindra, HCL Technologies and Infosys featuring among the top gainers on the Nifty 50, while concerns over artificial intelligence investments continued to weigh on US and Asian markets.

At around 9:20 am, the Nifty IT index was up 1.3 percent at 31,310.7, emerging as the strongest sectoral performer on the NSE. In contrast, the Sensex declined 108.9 points, or 0.13 percent, to 82,912.8, while the Nifty fell 33.2 points to 25,481.1.

The gains in IT stocks stood out amid broad-based selling pressure, with most sectoral indices trading lower. The Nifty Metal index plunged 2.11 percent, while Nifty Energy and Nifty PSU Bank declined 1.02 percent each. The Nifty Consumer Durables index slipped 0.80 percent.

TCS, Tech Mahindra, HCL Tech among top Nifty gainers

Large-cap IT stocks advanced despite the weakness in benchmark indices. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) gained 1.53 percent to Rs 2,378.60, making it one of the top five gainers on the Nifty 50.

  • Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

Tech Mahindra rose 0.93 percent to Rs 1,739.10, while HCL Technologies advanced 0.88 percent to Rs 1,344.60. Infosys climbed 0.47 percent to Rs 1,097, placing four major IT companies among the top 10 Nifty gainers.

The gains were not confined to large-cap stocks, with several midcap IT companies recording even stronger advances.

Midcap IT stocks rally; LT Technology, Persistent jump 3%

Midcap technology stocks also attracted buying interest, with six IT companies featuring among the top 10 midcap gainers on the BSE.

LT Technology Services and Persistent Systems gained around 3 percent each, while Coforge climbed 2.8 percent. Mphasis advanced 2.1 percent, followed by Tata Elxsi, up 1.4 percent, and Hexaware Technologies, which gained 1.3 percent.

The widespread gains across large-cap and midcap IT stocks contrasted with weakness in the broader market. The Nifty Midcap 100 declined 0.43 percent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 slipped 0.54 percent.

Indian IT stocks defy global technology selloff

The rally in Indian IT shares came against a sharply negative global backdrop, with technology and semiconductor stocks under pressure following a disappointing broader market response to Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering.

On Thursday, the Nasdaq Composite plunged 2.25 percent to 23,879.2, while the S&P 500 fell 2.02 percent to 7,175.83, extending its losing streak to six consecutive sessions.

Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI chatbot, raised $81.31 billion in the world's largest IPO. Its shares surged as much as 38.6 percent above the offer price during their market debut but pared gains to close 17.1 percent higher.

Despite the strong listing, the IPO failed to restore confidence in the broader AI investment trade, with investors continuing to reassess technology valuations and the sustainability of massive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The selling extended into Asian markets on Friday. South Korea's KOSPI plunged 4.7 percent, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell more than 4 percent. Japanese technology companies were among the hardest hit, with SoftBank Group, Kioxia Holdings and Ibiden tumbling more than 10 percent each during morning trading.

data.title: Coinbase backs CFTC proposal to distinguish prediction market contracts from gambling
data.description:
Crypto exchange Coinbase has filed comments supporting the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission's proposals to explicitly include event contracts in the definition of a "swap" and separate them from casino-style gambling products, as federal regulators and states remain locked in legal disputes over jurisdiction of prediction markets.

In a letter submitted Wednesday, Coinbase said that event contracts — including contracts based on sports, politics, culture, and weather — already qualify as swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA).

The company argued that event contracts are tradeable financial instruments whose value and payment depend on future events, and that they can help market participants "hedge real economic risks."

"Making that treatment explicit will provide important certainty in an area where state actions and conflicting judicial decisions have created unnecessary confusion," the company said.

Distinguishing event contracts

In a separate letter, Coinbase backed the CFTC's interim rule to exclude casino-style gambling products from the "swap" definition. The company said such gambling products are neither tradable nor cleared and were "never indicated" by Congress to fall within the definition of swap.

"Casino games and sportsbook wagers are not derivatives, and they have long been regulated by the states and tribes," the company added.

Coinbase argued that exchange-traded event contracts are "fundamentally distinct" from sportsbooks traditionally regulated under state laws.

"An event-contract exchange serves as a neutral market operator," the company said. "[It] does not choose prices or act as a counterparty to its members' trades, and it is indifferent to whether any given customer wins or loses."

Coinbase's comments were in response to the CFTC's proposal and interim final rule released last month, which were open for public comment through Nov. 18.

Legal battles intensify

Federal regulators and state authorities have been embroiled in escalating legal battles over who has the authority to regulate prediction market platforms. The CFTC has maintained that it has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction markets under the CEA, while several states have argued that certain event contracts violate state gambling laws.

During a Thursday interview at The Hill and The Block's Capitol Crypto Forum, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said the CFTC would work with the Justice Department to defend its jurisdiction when states sue prediction market platforms.

The CFTC and the DOJ sued Utah last month and filed lawsuits against Arkansas and Louisiana last week.

"If it's a legal and lawful derivative, it should be regulated by the market regulator. It's not something that goes to the state," Selig said.

data.title: Atomic Eagle Defines New Uranium Zone at Muntanga North in Zambia
data.description:
Atomic Eagle has defined a new uranium-mineralised zone and extended another at its Muntanga project in Zambia following a broad 2026 exploration campaign.

Follow-up drilling expanded Target 5 to approximately 1,500 metres by 200m, while Target 6 now contains a separate zone measuring about 800m by 200m.

The discoveries add to a regional program testing eight targets at Muntanga North and two at Namakande, although the results remain at the exploration stage.

With that campaign largely assessed, Atomic Eagle is redirecting drilling towards Chisebuka to support a revised mineral resource estimate and updated development studies.

The planned MRE could include upgrading suitable material into the Indicated category where drilling density and geological continuity provide sufficient confidence.

Two Zones Take Shape

At Target 5, follow-up drilling traced a shallow-dipping mineralised horizon broadly parallel to the host rock layers, with geological structures potentially influencing its distribution.

Target 6 produced a coherent zone averaging roughly 3m in thickness and remaining open at its interpreted boundaries, although further assessment will be needed to determine whether additional drilling is warranted.

Notable Target 6 results included 5.2m at 380 parts per million equivalent uranium oxide from 38.8m and 10.9m at 250ppm equivalent uranium oxide from 36.8m.

The results are derived from downhole gamma measurements rather than laboratory assays, with radiometric readings converted into estimated uranium grades using calibrated equipment and project-specific factors.

Atomic Eagle considers the near-vertical drill intersections approximately representative of true widths because the mineralised layers dip gently, but further verification work remains necessary.

Regional Drilling Refines Targets

Since its September exploration update, the group has drilled 84 holes covering 8,367m across Targets 5 to 8, taking regional drilling at Muntanga North and Namakande to 216 holes totalling 21,829m during 2026.

However, Targets 1 to 4, 7, and 8 produced no significant uranium mineralisation, despite radiometric anomalies identified at surface during the targeting program.

Atomic Eagle interprets some of those responses as potentially reflecting the movement of radioactive material along fractures and rock layers rather than substantial mineralisation immediately beneath the anomalies.

The unsuccessful holes will inform the geological model, but management does not currently consider them sufficient grounds for follow-up drilling at those particular targets.

Chisebuka Diamond Program

Infill and extension drilling has resumed at Chisebuka, where 12 reverse circulation holes have been completed to check grades inferred from gamma logging, with laboratory assays still pending.

A further 25 diamond drill holes are planned to provide samples for assays and metallurgical test work, alongside additional down-the-hole drilling to evaluate known mineralisation and selected extensions.

“The 2026 program has tested a broad portfolio of regional targets and continued to identify uranium mineralisation across the Muntanga licences, [and] has added materially to our geological understanding,” chief executive officer Phil Hoskins said.

“At several targets, drilling at the centre of coincident radiometric and soil anomalies intersected evidence of uranium mobility or mineralisation indicating that additional mineralisation may occur nearby along strike, down dip or beneath cover—these interpretations will be tested in future exploration campaigns.”

Atomic Eagle will integrate the regional drilling results with geological, structural, and radiometric datasets before deciding which Muntanga North targets merit further resource-definition work.

data.title: India's 3i Infotech bags bank IT contract
data.description:
Indian IT services company 3i Infotech (BSE: 532628) has secured a three-year purchase order worth INR244.8mn ($2.623mn) from a domestic bank, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 19.

The order, dated the same day, comes from a new customer. The contract puts 3i Infotech in charge of running and maintaining IT systems across the lender's entire operation, from its data centre and disaster recovery environment to its head office and branch network.

The company did not name the bank and said confidentiality obligations prevented it from doing so. Under the order, 3i Infotech will provide IT facility management services covering the operation and maintenance of the bank's IT infrastructure, services, applications and systems software.

The work also includes full onsite annual maintenance of IT equipment and software, software and security subscriptions, infrastructure support and ISO certification services. The committed term begins on January 1, 2027, and runs for three years. The two parties may agree to extend it, according to the filing.

The value of INR244.8mn excludes applicable taxes. The company described the customer as a domestic entity. It said neither its promoter nor its promoter group or group companies hold any interest in the bank, and that the order does not count as a related party transaction.

data.title: Gold price crash: Yellow metal and silver slump over 4% each on MCX
data.description:
Gold and silver continue to fall under further pressure as precious and base metals slump under pressure as the US dollar strengthens, amid rising worries of a rate hike from the US Federal Reserve.

GOLD, SILVER FALL

Here in India, the precious metals are facing the pinch as well. On MCX, the Multi Commodity Exchange of India Limited (MCX), which is India's largest commodity derivatives exchange, Gold fell nearly 4% to ₹1.22 lakh/10 gram. In addition, silver on MCX fell nearly 6%, slumping to ₹1.48 lakh/kg at the opening of the day's trade.

On the global scale, as per Reuters, spot gold dropped 1.9% to $3,551.68 per ounce, after touching its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. Bullion was down about 8.9% for the week, marking its sharpest weekly fall since the week of March 20. US gold futures for December delivery declined 3.6% to $3,551.90.

Asian shares fell on Friday and were set for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic’s debut did little to revive investor confidence in the AI sector.

The dollar remained close to a 19-month peak on Friday, extending its recent gains and making bullion priced in greenbacks more costly for buyers using other currencies.

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday that the Fed would need to raise rates again because inflation remained too high. She also said a shared understanding was more important than providing explicit guidance on the interest-rate outlook.

According to CME’s FedWatch tool, markets assign a 97.3% probability to a 25-basis-point US rate increase in December, while pricing in a 2.7% chance of a larger, 50-basis-point move.

Higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding bullion, which does not generate yield, and therefore make it less attractive to investors.

data.title: HSBC picks private banks, industrials and capital goods in India as markets broaden beyond AI
data.description:
Herald van der Linde, Head of Equity Strategy-Asia Pacific at HSBC, expects volatility in AI-linked markets to continue as investors reassess valuations and adjust their concentrated positions.

HSBC recently upgraded India to an overweight stance, pointing out that India's improving earnings outlook, more reasonable large-cap valuations and significant underweight positions among global funds make the market more attractive than it was six months ago.

In India, Herald van der Linde sees opportunities in large-cap stocks, particularly private sector banks, industrials and capital goods companies, including ports and cement makers. He also expects global interest rates to remain under upward pressure over the next six months amid inflation concerns.

[faq type="interview" title="This is an edited transcript of the interview."][ques][/ques][ans][/ans][/faq][faq type="interview"][ques]What do you make of India's outperformance compared to Korean indices amid the unraveling of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade?[/ques][ans]No, I'm not quite sure it will truly unravel. But there are quite a few positions that need to be readjusted because we've seen incredibly concentrated bets throughout 2026. Most of the market's performance in the US, but also in Asia, came from a handful of stocks. What does this mean for India? We have actually upgraded India to overweight about two or three weeks ago for exactly these reasons. We felt that India's story in itself looked much better. In particular, we were looking for something other than AI. We thought markets would broaden out, and that's something we had already anticipated, perhaps around the middle of this year. So, we moved India from underweight to neutral at the time. But a couple of weeks ago, as I said, we moved to overweight for exactly that reason.[/ans][/faq][faq type="interview"][ques]How much of this adjustment in the AI trade is done, and how much is left?[/ques][ans]That's a very good question, and it's difficult to answer. I do think the markets are trying to find what the new normal for AI is. You can take a couple of views. You can say it's going to go back to where it used to be, that the new normal is what the old normal was and the markets will rally back. That's very unlikely, in my view, but it's a scenario you can think of. You can also say this is going to unravel, it's all over, and it's going to go back to where we were five years ago or something like that. That's probably also unlikely. AI will stay with us. It's a new growth industry, so we're going to be somewhere in between. I know these are two very big extremes, but we're going to be somewhere in between. The market is trying to figure out what valuations we need to attach to an industry that is growing fairly rapidly, although that growth will probably slowdown in the future. That's what the market is trying to find out, and we don't know how that's going to happen. It's going to take a bit of time, maybe a year or so. In that time, we're going to have quite a bit of volatility. However, in the near term, there's still a lot of positioning that needs to be readjusted. Everybody was in the same stocks in the US, but also in Asia. It was SK Hynix, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturng Co (TSMC) and Samsung at the beginning of this year. These positions need to be adjusted, and that will take a bit of time. So, that's going to put some downward pressure on some of these stocks.[/ans][/faq]

data.title: Paytm share price can still test ₹2,300 levels, Nomura says despite MDR uncertainty
data.description:
Shares of One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, gained on Friday, November 20, after it said its unit is looking at investing up to ₹200 crore into a Singapore-based firm.

Paytm, in an exchange filing on Thursdsay, said its step-down wholly-owned subsidiary Paytm Singapore Pte Ltd's board has approved the partnership with Funding Asia Group Pte Ltd (Funding Societies) to invest up to ₹200 crore into subsidiaries of the latter. This includes an initial all-cash investment of approximately ₹162 crore for a 19.1% stake in CardUp Pte Ltd, Funding Societies' payment subsidiary.

The acquisition is indicated to be completed by May 20, 2027.

The remaining investment of around ₹38 crore will be made in one of the affiliates of the Singapore firm. The proposed investments are subject to confirmatory due diligence, customary corporate approvals, execution of definitive documents and any regulatory approvals, the exchange filing said.

In addition to this, Paytm will also enter into business and technology partnership with CardUp, under which the former will provide payments and lending technology to the latter to expand its technology-led payments and financial services stack in Singapore.

The company said this is in-line with its previously disclosed roadmap to expand its presence in select international markets via the 'partner operated' model, where Paytm provides its proven acceptance platform and innovative devices, while the local partner leads sales, distribution and on-ground operations to serve merchants. Paytm said it will monetise its contributions via licensing fees, revneue-sharing and other arrangements, while deploying limited capital.

Nomura Remains Bullish

Global investment banking firm Nomura is of the view that the investment is small, relative to Paytm's balance sheet and is unlikely to change its financials materially in the near-term. It thinks it is a low-cost way to enter the Singapore market.

Nomura has a "buy" recommendation and target price of ₹2,300 per share on the Paytm stock. This indicates an upside of 32.2% from its previous closing price.

Nomura said Paytm's ₹200 crore investment plan is part of the earlier 500 crore it invested into Paytm Singapore. Of this, the ₹160 crore is an all-cash investment for the 19.1% stake in CardUp.

Paytm, in its exchange filing, also added that in continuation to its earlier disclosure on October 26, 2026, it has completed the additional investment of ₹500 crore in its wholly-owned subsidiary Paytm Cloud Technologies Ltd (PCTL).

Subsequently, PCTL has also completed an additional investment of ₹500 crore in its wholly-owned subsidiary Paytm Singapore, a step-down wholly-owned subsidiary of the company.

Why Paytm Shares Fell On Thursday?

Shares of Paytm fell 9% to ₹1,725.9 apiece in the previous trading session. The stock was down, along with its peers Pine Labs and One MobiKwik after CNBC-TV18 reported that the rollout date for the merchant discount rate (MDR) was still unclear.

Sources said the business-to-business payments via UPI could see a separate pricing structure, with a flat 5 charge proposed for merchant-to-merchant transactions. However, sources added that the NPCI UPI and Services steering committee had cleared the proposal around a month ago but the decisions has yet to be formally notified.

Out of the 24 analysts who have coverage on Paytm, 20 have a "buy" rating and four others have a "hold" rating. No analysts tracking the stock has a "sell" rating on it. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 16% from current levels.

Shares of Paytm are up 1.7% on Friday after Thursday's sell-off, currently trading at ₹1,755. The stock is still up 36% so far this year.

data.title: Neugebauer: Texas Court Ruling on Fermi's 70/30 Boardroom Maneuver Is a Loss for 100% of Texas Shareholders
data.description:
• Neugebauer: Under this ruling, the board can entrench itself with one quick vote, while shareholders need 70% of all outstanding shares to fight back.
  • Neugebauer: "That isn't Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."
  • Directors who failed to win a majority on October 30 are still sitting in the boardroom.
  • Neugebauer filing appeal because Texas's standing as the best place to do business in America depends on getting this right.
  • Texan voters have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them.

DALLAS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Toby Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc. (d/b/a Fermi America) (Nasdaq: FRMI) ("Fermi" or the "Company"), today issued the following statement after the Texas Business Court dismissed his claims in Neugebauer v. Fermi Inc. challenging the 70% supermajority bylaw the Company's board adopted in May without a shareholder vote.

"This isn't just a loss for Melissa and me. I believe it's a loss for every shareholder of every Texas company," said Toby Neugebauer. "Under this ruling, a board can change the rules in the middle of a fight, without a shareholder vote. It takes the board one quick vote to change the rules. It takes shareholders 70% of all outstanding shares to have a voice. Do the math. A little over 30% can block anything, and a share that is never voted counts as a no.

"Directors who could not win a majority of the shareholder support are still sitting in the boardroom. I don't think that is Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."

On May 13, 2026, in the middle of a shareholder contest, Fermi's board amended the Company's bylaws. Under the amendment, shareholders now need 70% of all outstanding shares to expand the board or change how the bylaws are amended. The board, however, can change those same rules with a simple majority vote of its directors. In August, the board changed director elections to require a majority of all outstanding shares, with unvoted shares counting as a no vote. At the October 30 annual meeting, neither director on the ballot reached that majority. Both men remain on the board.

"I'm proud of the work Texas has done to become the best place in America to do business," Neugebauer continued. "But capital flows to boards that answer to their owners. If shareholders can be silenced whenever a board disagrees with them, investors will notice."

This November, voters rejected the insider, pay-to-play politics that has harmed Fermi. Texans have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them. We respectfully disagree with the Court and feel confident that we will be successful on appeal, because this isn't how good governance works.

Texas earned its business reputation. Now it has to protect it. I will continue to advocate for good governance, not for financial gain, but for the good of Texas.

SOURCE Toby Neugebauer

data.title: Nifty opens lower as global tech selloff offsets domestic gains; Max Healthcare, Apollo top gainers
data.description:
Equity benchmarks opened in the red on Friday, November 20, 2026, dragged down by a broad-based selloff on Wall Street overnight, even as domestic market internals remained relatively firm. The Sensex, which had closed the previous session at 83,021.75, opened at 82,558.25 and was trading at 82,864.08, down 157.67 points or 0.19 per cent. The Nifty 50, which had closed Thursday at 25,514.30, opened at 25,368.00 and was trading at 25,447.95, down 66.35 points or 0.26 per cent at 9.18 am.

Asian markets follow Wall Street lower

The gap-down open came as GIFT Nifty had signalled a roughly 200-point fall at the start of trade, in line with steep declines across Asian markets. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell over 4.5 per cent and South Korea’s KOSPI shed 4.3 per cent, as investors unwound positions in AI-linked technology stocks across the region.

The trigger was a punishing session on Wall Street on Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 1,101 points, or 2.19 per cent, to close at 49,097, its worst level since early June and below the 50,000 mark for the first time in months. The S&P 500 fell 2.02 per cent to 7,175, marking its sixth consecutive daily loss, while the Nasdaq shed 2.25 per cent to 23,879. Paradoxically, Anthropic’s initial public offering, which debuted at a $2 trillion valuation and closed 17 per cent above its $83 issue price, failed to lift sentiment. “Anthropic’s strong listing failed to allay concerns over stretched AI valuations and debt-financed technology spending,” said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth.

Healthcare, cement stocks gain; Titan leads losers

Among the Nifty 50 top gainers, Max Healthcare led with a gain of 2.93 per cent, last trading at ₹1,071.15 against a previous close of ₹1,040.65. Apollo Hospitals rose 2.01 per cent to ₹8,914.00, while UltraTech Cement advanced 1.70 per cent to ₹12,773.00. TCS gained 1.36 per cent to ₹2,374.60 and HCL Technologies added 0.95 per cent to reach ₹1,345.60.

On the losing side, Titan fell the most, dropping 2.38 per cent to ₹4,588.00 from a previous close of ₹4,700.00. JSW Steel declined 2.36 per cent to ₹1,305.20, while Larsen & Toubro shed 1.76 per cent to ₹4,136.70. Tata Steel fell 1.75 per cent to ₹177.72, and Shriram Finance lost 1.73 per cent to ₹956.50.

Metal stocks under pressure; FIIs extend buying streak

The sectoral picture reflected the global narrative. Metals were under pressure following sharp falls in international commodity prices. “The sharp correction in metal prices has attracted buying in auto stocks and consumer durables,” said Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. Healthcare and cement counters held firm, buoyed by domestic demand optimism, while IT stocks remained subdued, an extension of Thursday’s trend when the Nifty IT index fell 1.1 per cent.

Banking and financial stocks continued to find support from sustained foreign institutional investor buying. FIIs had purchased equities worth ₹7,411 crore on November 19, their eighth consecutive session of net buying. “The bulk of the FII flows have gone into financial services, particularly banking majors... FIIs are now buying the very same stocks they have been selling to raise money for the AI trade,” Vijayakumar noted. Domestic institutional investors, however, remained net sellers for a second straight session, offloading ₹1,356 crore worth of equities.

Gold and silver slide; dollar index rises

Gold and silver markets offered little comfort. MCX December gold was trading at ₹1,22,435 per 10 grams at 9:04 am IST, down ₹5,017 or 3.94 per cent, while December silver fell ₹9,448, or 6 per cent, to ₹1,48,034 per kg. “For someone buying 20 grams of gold, the MCX decline represents a ₹10,034 reduction in the futures benchmark,” said Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus. Internationally, COMEX December gold futures were at $3,551.90 per ounce, down 3.6 per cent, with silver at $42.44 per ounce, down 4.33 per cent.

The US dollar index, buoyed by hawkish Federal Reserve signals and expectations of a December rate hike, rose for an eighth straight session to 103.96. The 10-year US Treasury yield stood at approximately 5.05 per cent. Crude oil remained broadly stable, with WTI around $82.50 and Brent near $92 per barrel.

Nifty support levels in focus

Analysts said the market’s ability to defend key support levels would be decisive for the day’s trajectory. “Nifty needs to hold the 25,300–25,350 zone to preserve Thursday’s breakout structure,” said Radhakrishnan. Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Neo, pegged immediate support at 25,400 and 25,320, with resistance at 25,650 and 25,700. “A break below 25,200 could weaken the structure and drag the indices back towards the 25,100–25,000 zone,” he said.

data.title: NetEase, Kuaishou Shares Plunge After 3Q Results Miss Estimates
data.description:
By Megan Cheah

Shares of Chinese internet companies NetEase and Kuaishou Technology fell Friday after their respective quarterly results missed consensus estimates.

NetEase's Hong Kong-listed stock plunged as much as 20% to 150.30 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$19.16, before paring losses to trade 18% lower. The stock remains on track for its largest one-day percentage decline since 2023, according to LSEG data.

Its American depository receipts closed 11% lower overnight.

Meanwhile, Kuaishou shares shed as much as 13% to HK$19.97, marking a record intraday low for the stock. It has since recouped some losses to trade 10% lower.

Earnings of both companies released Thursday failed to meet analysts' consensus projections. NetEase, China's second-largest gaming company, reported a 2.6% on-year decline in quarterly profit to 8.40 billion yuan, equivalent to $1.26 billion, versus market expectations of 9.45 billion yuan.

Analysts noted that softer-than-expected games segment revenue was the main drag on results. Growth in China's gaming market has moderated in the second half of the year following a strong start, partly due to a high base for PC games and a lack of blockbuster releases during the critical summer holiday season.

Despite the results miss, analysts at Citi and Nomura remain moderately optimistic about NetEase's outlook, pointing to the company's upcoming game title, "Ananta," slated for release in early 2027, as a potential key catalyst for future growth and revenue.

Meanwhile, short video platform operator Kuaishou swung to a wider-than-expected loss in the third quarter, weighed down by intense external competition and a changing consumer environment.

Citi analysts expressed a more cautious view on Kuaishou's prospects amid a tougher macroeconomic backdrop, intensified competition, and platform traffic pressures.

"We see limited visibility on Kuaishou's topline and profit trajectory ahead, though its net cash position could provide share price support," they said.

Write to Megan Cheah at megan.cheah@wsj.com

data.title: China's $2 billion bond draws large orders, prices in line with US Treasuries
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bond attracts over $72 billion in orders, 36 times covered
  • Deal marks China's second dollar bond priced at zero premium
  • Strong demand shows investors look past geopolitical tensions, source says

By Scott Murdoch and Yantoultra Ngui

A $2 billion bond from China was priced in line with Treasuries instead of initial guidance of a 25-basis-point premium, after attracting orders worth more than $72 billion, according to a bookrunner's message seen by Reuters on Friday.

The deal for the 3-year debt, which was 36 times oversubscribed, marks the second that China has carried out at a zero premium after it also raised $2 billion in a 3-year bond last year.

"China is viewed as a relatively safe credit supported by low external debt and abundant foreign reserves, even as economic challenges persist," said Gary Ng, senior economist at Natixis.

"Limited dollar bond supply from China and steady demand from offshore Chinese entities also helped shape the dynamics."

Bookbuilding was carried out as Chinese President Xi Jinping met with US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Xi and Trump also met separately on the sidelines of the APEC forum on Thursday. Xi said relations between China and the US had been stable and on a positive trajectory.

The strength of the demand shows that domestic and international investors were willing to overlook geopolitical tensions between China and the US, according to a person who worked on the transaction.

The person was not permitted to speak to media and declined to be identified.

More than 590 investors placed orders, with buyers from Asia accounting for more than 52% of them, the bookrunner's message showed. Central banks and sovereign wealth funds were the most active buyers.

China's Ministry of Finance confirmed the deal in a statement on Friday.

China is not a major issuer of dollar-denominated debt. It raised $6 billion in 2024 and 2025 after a two-year hiatus, Dealogic figures showed.

data.title: NVDA Stock Down 40% From October Peak Amid China Spying Crisis: California Begins Probe Into Chip Sales
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia reportedly sought U.S. approval early this year to sell more than 40,000 H200 chips to a company tied to Megaspeed and Alice Huang, according to The New York Times.
  • Nvidia is in late-stage talks to buyout AI firm Inflection for more than $500 million, The Information reported.
  • NVDA stock dipped 1.6% in Thursday’s overnight session.

Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) stock is heading for its seventh consecutive week in the red, with shares dropping another 1.6% in overnight trading late Thursday amid news that California opened an investigation into whether former CEO Jensen Huang’s actions allowed China to obtain advanced AI technology and misled investors.

“My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of law,” California's Attorney General Rob Bonta said in an X post on Thursday.

“Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors.”

The development is the latest in a major upheaval at the AI chipmaker. Investors are reassessing their positions in a post-Huang era, amid daily updates on his and Nvidia’s dealings with Megaspeed, a suspected Chinese spy outfit, the search for a new CEO, and probes by authorities.

Nvidia Fallout: New Updates

Lawmakers released confidential information on Thursday showing that the Commerce Department had approved the sale of more than 800,000 advanced AI chips to Chinese companies for the year, as of May, including several firms on a list of Chinese military companies maintained by the Pentagon, according to a report in The New York Times.

Nvidia also reportedly submitted an application to sell more than 40,000 H200 chips to a company tied to Megaspeed and Alice Huang, the executive whom authorities suspect is a Chinese asset.

Meanwhile, The Information reported that Nvidia was in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for more than $500 million, adding that talks began before Huang's departure.

The outlet describes Inception as "a two-year-old startup that develops a type of AI that aims to perform faster than the one that powers products such as ChatGPT and Claude."

Crisis Deepens 

Huang’s disclosure last week of an extramarital affair plunged Nvidia fueled a sharp selloff in the company’s shares and resulted in his ouster as CEO. NVDA stock is now down 40% from its peak in early October and 21% year to date.

The crisis has weighed on the company as well as the broader AI trade, with key AI-linked stocks falling on Thursday despite a strong initial public offering by Anthropic (ANT).

“Nvidia is casting a pall on the market that’s tainting everything,” CNBC analyst Jim Cramer said on his show “Mad Money.” Despite blockbuster earnings earlier this week, Nvidia appears to be struggling to regain investors’ confidence in the wake of Huang’s exit, with Cramer arguing that Huang’s desire to return could further complicate Nvidia’s search for a permanent CEO.

The continued chatter about a potential Huang return “makes it so that this still-giant company is sinking like a stone, destroying the savings of millionaires and regular index investors alike,” Cramer said.

Retail View On NVDA

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA dipped but remained ‘extremely bullish.’

“$NVDA one of the largest companies in the entire world is down almost $100 a share within a month, with record breaking earnings and record-breaking guidance; down about 42%,” wrote a trader. “There are going to be millionaires made from today. Easiest gain of wealth since COVID.”

Another said, “$NVDA literally just down due to dumb articles that have 0 impact on the business. The company already guided earnings that assume no revenue from China.”
